Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: The National Identity Cards Act 2011 (NICA) is specifically a digital/biometric ID regulation. It mandates an electronic National Identity Register, biometric data collection (fingerprints, photo), chip/barcode on ID cards, and electronic access via API. Supported by Communications (SIM/Device Registration) Regulations 2021.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed against the primary statute (LesLII text of NICA 2011), which establishes an electronic National Identity Register with biometric capture and chip/barcode cards, and corroborated by an independent CIPESA legal brief on the Communications (SIM/Mobile Device Registration) Regulations 2021, which link SIM registration biometrics to the National Identity and Civil Registry. No newer regulation found (2024 Amendment Bill concerns card expiry only, not digital-ID-specific rules). Value Code 2 (Yes) confirmed.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: NICA 2011 Section 13: Eligible persons are those aged 16 years and older, either citizens or non-citizens with an indefinite residence permit. Birth registration covered by separate civil registry system. Unique ID number assigned at birth and printed on birth certificate but NID card issued from age 16.

revision_notes: Confirmed via primary legislation (LesLII, NICA 2011 s.13 and s.9(6)(u)-(v)): eligibility/credential age is 16. On the metadata scale (1=>17; 2=10-17; 3=6-10; 4=1-5; 5=<1), age 16 falls in the '10-17' bracket, which is Value Code 2 — not '6-10' (Value Code 3) as originally recorded. The original Value Code/Value Name was inconsistent with its own cited evidence; corrected to 2.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Section 16 NICA 2011 mandates use of the national identity card to access all services, making enrollment de facto compulsory. Enrollment itself is not explicitly legally mandated but exclusion from services acts as strong compulsion. Some entities (e.g., Electoral Commission) allow alternative documents in practice.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed via primary text (LesLII, NICA 2011 s.16): 'No person who is eligible to have an identity card shall access all services unless the person produces his or her identity card.' This creates de facto compulsion via service exclusion rather than a direct legal duty to enrol, consistent with 'Mandatory for some' (Value Code 2). No newer legislation changes this position (2024 Amendment Bill addresses card expiry only). Value Code 2 confirmed.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: NICA 2011 Section 13 explicitly includes non-citizens holding an indefinite residence permit as eligible for the national identity card (aged 16+). Refugees and temporary residents are not covered. This is a meaningful but limited inclusion of non-nationals.
